notesStmt.note: Whitman dated a corrected proof of this poem reads "Oct 17 '84." The present draft was, therefore, written between October 10 (the date of the letter on the reverse) and October 17, 1884.
"Of That Blithe Throat of Thine" which was first published in the January 1885 issue of Harper's Monthly Magazine. It was later included in November Boughs (1888).

lg.head: Of that blithe throat of thine

note.p: [More than 83 degrees north—about a good day's steaming distance to the Pole by one of our fast oceaners, in clear water—Greeley heard the song of a ‸single snow⹀bird merrily sounding out of over the desolation.]

lg.l:
Of that blithe throat of thine, through mid from ‸arctic bleak
and blank

I‸'ll mind the lesson, arctic solitary bird—I also —let me too welcome
ice and chilling drifts

Nay, E'en the profoundest chill as now—a torpid
heart, pulse, a brain, unnerv'd

Old age land⹀lock'ed within its winter⹀bay, (cold,
cold, O cold!)
These snowy hairs, lameness, a feeble arm,

For them ‸thy faith, thy rule I I'll to take, and grave it to
the last

Not mid for the summery's zones alone— not
chants of youth alone or souths ‸warm tides alone,

But held by sluggish floes, pack'd in the
northern ice the cumulus of years,
S These All Now These—with gay heart I also these too I to I'll also sing.
